newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel blames Palestinians for killing land dealer.
newsitem.headline: Israel blames Palestinians for killing land dealer.

text.p: Israeli officials blamed the Palestinian Authority on Saturday for the shooting death of an Arab known to have sold land to Jews.

Ali Mohammed Jumhour, 34, was the third land dealer found dead in the West Bank since Palestinian Justice Minister Freih Abu Medeen was quoted in a report published on May 4 as saying that Palestinians who sold land to Jews faced execution.

"The body of a land dealer was found near Ramallah. He was most probably killed for having been a land dealer. He was shot in the head," said police spokeswoman Linda Menuhin, adding the man was an Israeli citizen.
Israel's Public Security Minister Avigdor Kahalani said he ordered police to give the investigation top priority.
"We are speaking about a murder of an Israeli Arab carried out by people that are low and cowardly. The signs point to the Palestinian Authority," Kahalani said.
Palestinian police have refused to comment.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's media adviser Shai Bazak accused Palestinian officials of backing the killing of land dealers. He said this put into question the Palestinian Authority's commitment to peace with Israel.

"Preliminary investigations indicate he was investigated by Palestinian police at the start of last week. They explained to him that his fate would be similar to that of land dealer Farid Bashiti," Menuhin said.
Bashiti, 70, of Jerusalem, was found dead in PLO-ruled Ramallah earlier in May. His funeral was repeatedly delayed and the burial site changed out of fear of violence.
Another dealer, Harbi Abu Sarah, in his 60s, was found shot dead near Ramallah and buried in his home village of Ain Yabrud nearby.

"The murder of land dealers is carried out with the full backing of top level officials in the Palestinian Authority and places a big question mark over the Authority's willingness for peaceful relations with Israel," Bazak said.
Abu Medeen said at a news conference in Ramallah last Tuesday the PLO was interrogating "seven to 12" Palestinians on suspicion of selling land to Israelis.
Abu Medeen warned Arabs with Israeli citizenship that they too could face the death penalty if caught selling land to Jews.
"I warn and advise those Palestinians who have become Israeli citizens that this will not protect them. They will be tried in one way or another," he told reporters.
Washington and an international human rights group have urged Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to forbid retribution against land dealers.

The PLO has said the ban on selling land to Jews was necessary to halt the expansion of Jewish settlements in the West Bank, Gaza Strip and Arab East Jerusalem, occupied by Israel since the 1967 Middle East war.
Palestinians see settlements as an Israeli attempt to thwart their goal of founding an independent state in those areas.
The Palestinian Authority controls parts of the West Bank and Gaza Strip under a 1993 self-rule with Israel. Palestinian police are limited to operating in areas under their rule.
Israel has called the ban "racist" and linked it with the deaths of Bashiti and Abu Sarah. The PLO denies the charges.
